items.text: WTI down 2% w/w to $84.25, Brent -2% to $91.82, yet near-term volatility risk remains acute after July 7 Iran strikes resumption. Energy shocks have driven 250bp of BoE/ECB tightening since May, and sticky PPI at 5.51% (down only 46bp YoY) signals pass-through risk in credit—especially for leveraged energy names and suppliers dependent on stable feedstock costs.

Payrolls collapsed to +57K in June (consensus ≈+130K), with jobless claims rising to 197K last week. Unemployment at 4.2% masks wage growth of 3.52% (up 13bp)—classic late-cycle wage-price spiral signal. For credit investors, watch for mass layoff announcements; labor tightness still constrains corporate margin expansion despite cooling demand.

Core inflation moderated nicely (2.57% YoY, -25bp m/m), but headline PCE 3.67% and core PCE 3.29% remain well above Fed's 2% target. UST10Y down 4bp to 4.67% (curve up 9bp to 45bp steeper), while HY OAS widened 8bp to 287. Sticky core + weak payrolls = recession fears, yet market still prices ~3 more hikes; any pivot would compress spreads abruptly.

Michigan Consumer Sentiment preliminary July reading rose to 54.4, up 9.9% m/m, driven by falling gas prices, but remains down 12% YoY and near all-time lows. June retail sales ex-auto 6.95% YoY, down from 7.92%, hints at consumer deceleration. GDP nowcast at 4.95% vs 1.5% realized Q2; distortion likely inflates near-term growth optics for credit.

CCC OAS jumped 17bp to 1013, HY at 287 (up 8bp), IG stable at 81bp—compression in IG masks festering stress in high-yield and distressed. Mortgage rates 6.66% (+8bp), existing home sales down 2.4% to 4.09M SAAR, housing starts bounced to 1427K but demand fragility persists. Refinancing risk elevated for floating-rate issuers.

China manufacturing PMI fell to 49.2 in July from 50.3, marking a return to contraction after brief expansion. Composite PMI declined to 49.3, lowest since pandemic restrictions ended in 2022. Credit spillover risk for commodity exporters, shipping financials, and commodity-linked PE assets; watch Asian HY spreads for contagion.

ECB held rates steady at 2.25% deposit rate in July, while markets price 88% probability of 25bp hike in September. ECB's Lagarde emphasized June hike was not insurance but response to genuine inflation challenge, with 2% target return only by late 2027 if policy becomes more restrictive. Divergence between Fed (hold/pivot), ECB (more hikes likely), and BoE (pause risk) creates cross-border credit dislocations.

themeCards.title: Middle East Energy Shock
themeCards.statusLine: July 7 US strikes on Iran resumed; WTI/Brent moderately lower but geopolitical volatility remains. PPI sticky at 5.51%, input costs elevated across manufacturing.
themeCards.relevance: Energy pass-through into credit prices for leveraged energy, shipping, industrials. CRE energy tenants and commodity-linked collateral at risk if sustained spike occurs. Hedging demand supports derivatives costs.

themeCards.title: China Demand Collapse
themeCards.statusLine: Composite PMI at 49.3, lowest since 2022 reopening; manufacturing slowdown driven by sharp drop in new orders. Domestic demand remains the biggest drag.
themeCards.relevance: Significant spillover to commodity credit, shipping finance, and EM exporters. Refinance risk for China-linked issuers. Hard asset collateral values under pressure (iron ore, copper linked). Warrant watching for covenant stress and default waves in sector-wide credits.

themeCards.title: US Labor Market Shock
themeCards.statusLine: June payrolls only +57K (vs ~130K consensus), jobless claims rising, yet wage growth 3.52% persists. Unemployment 4.2% stable but breadth weak.
themeCards.relevance: Triggers recession fears and potential Fed pivot narrative. Spread compression on pause/cut bets conflicting with sticky inflation. For credit: mass layoff warnings loom; consumer refinancing stress building. Watch for covenant triggers (leverage, EBITDA) in consumer-exposed retailers and staffing.

themeCards.title: Tight Mortgage & Refi Wall
themeCards.statusLine: 30yr mortgage 6.66% (+8bp w/w), existing home sales down 2.4% YoY, housing starts volatile. Refinance cohort locked out.
themeCards.relevance: Legacy CMBS and MBS dislocation; HELOC drawdowns likely constrained. Residential mortgage originators squeezed. Credit risk in consumer-facing names dependent on home-equity lending and refi demand; housing-linked leveraged loans under pressure.

themeCards.title: High-Yield Spread Widening
themeCards.statusLine: CCC OAS +17bp w/w to 1013bp; HY +8bp to 287. IG holding 81bp masks deterioration in low-credit sub-indices. Distress screens widening.
themeCards.relevance: Dispersion creating opportunity in BB/BBB part of capital structure; CCC/B risk repricing on growth concerns and covenant stress. Loan defaults and refinancing failures likely uptick in autumn. Credit-negative sector rotation for commodity/energy/leisure; watch for CLO stress signals.

themeCards.title: Rate/Inflation Regime Uncertainty
themeCards.statusLine: ECB likely to hike again in Sept; Fed/BoE on pause; UST curve 45bp (steepest in weeks). Inflation (core 2.57%) cooling but headline PCE 3.67% sticky. VIX 20.66 (+404bp).
themeCards.relevance: Cross-currency basis dislocations and hedging costs rising. Floating-rate credit and cap/floor spreads volatile. Covenant renegotiations may accelerate. Corporates with non-USD debt exposure facing basis widening; bank lending spreads likely to reprice if rates go lower than 3.5% Fed funds terminal.

regime.label: Mid-Cycle Shift
regime.detail: Cooling labor, sticky core inflation, widening HY spreads, geopolitical volatility, China demand shock—recession fears vs. inflation persistence creating regime fog for credit.
